newsitem.title: USA: Equity Oil takes partial Siberian writeoff.
newsitem.headline: Equity Oil takes partial Siberian writeoff.

text.p: Equity Oil Co said Monday that it will take a pretax charge of $5.25 million, equal to $3.2 million after taxes, to reflect a partial writeoff of its investment in an exploration project in Eastern Siberia.

It said the writeoff, effective September 30, has resulted in a restatement of third quarter results to show a loss of $2,760,271, or $0.22 per share, compared with previously reported net income of $578,804 or $0.04 per share. This leaves the company with a nine month loss of $1,939,215, or $0.15 per share, compared with previously reported net income of $1,369,860 or $0.11 per share.

Equity Oil said the writeoff is being taken because its 50 percent owned subsidiary, Symskaya Exploration Inc, has decided to not re-enter the Lemok No. 1 well in in an effort to reach its original, primary objective.
It said Symskaya has charged the costs of drilling the Lemok No. 1 to expense as of September 30, causing Equity Oil to writeoff its equity share of these costs, the company explained.
As reported earlier, drilling of the well was stopped at a depth of 14,102 feet due to mechanical problems prior to reaching the primary target, expected at 14,500 feet.

"Based on the data collected and analyzed to date, the company believes that the project remains prospective, and Symskaya is actively soliciting partners to participate in further exploration and fund the drilling of a second well at the project," Equity Oil said.

If Symskaya is unable to find funding for a second well and consequently decides to suspend operations at the project, "the company may be required to recognize an additional equity loss in Symskaya," it continued.
Equity Oil said its remaining investment in Symskaya was about $3.7 million as of September 30 1996."
In its October 14 earnings release, Equity Oil talked of the possability of a $9 million writeoff on the promject.
